stem: The diagram shows $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$. Each triangle has sides $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $4\,\mathrm{cm}$ and a $35^{\circ}$ angle that is not between those two sides.

options.text: The matching sides and non-included angle do not always make the triangles congruent.
The triangles are congruent from the two equal side lengths alone.
SSA is a congruence rule that covers every triangle pair with those matching parts.
The triangles are congruent because $35$ is the standout printed number in the diagram.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Two sides and a non-included angle can fit more than one triangle shape, so SSA does not guarantee congruence.

teacher.key_rationale: SSA is not a congruence test: the same two sides and non-included angle can belong to non-congruent triangles.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote IGCSE right-triangle template into two SSA triangles with 6 cm, 4 cm, 35°.
